sections.html: Corydoras armatus attains a maximum length of about 5 cm.

The type specimens originated from Peru (Rio Huallaga). The species is now also imported from Venezuela, where the specimens look exactly like their Peruvian cousins. A similar form originates from Brazil (Rio Abuna, near the border to Bolivia), and a second similar form comes from Peru (Rio Nanay).

Corydoras armatus belongs to the Corydoras species known to scientists for a very long time. It is the sixth described species of the genus, and the original description appeared in 1868. It appeared comparatively late in the hobby, in the 1990s, and is still a real rarity in the trade.

The specific name "armatus" means "weaponed, armed" and refers to the enormous dorsal spine. This spine makes the species almost unique, as only two other similar Corydoras are known.

One originates from Brazil (Rio Abuna, near the border to Bolivia). It was sometimes called "Corydoras dorsalis" and "Corydoras ogawae"; both names have no scientific relevance. This form has been given the number CW86. It can hardly be distinguished from the "real" C. armatus by coloration or any other feature, except the 2,500 km distance between the Rio Huallaga and the Rio Abuna and the larger spots on the body of CW86.

The second sibling species comes from Peru (Rio Nanay) and has the C-number C96. It can be easily recognized by a black stripe over the shoulder, right below the dorsal fin.

The fish from Venezuela were freshly imported as healthy, large specimens.
